conviction_note: The bar sits on the company's own Q3 framing: about 27% growth, so about $104m against a $103.9m consensus. Over a rebuilt base rate of real prints (+22.4, +1.3, -5.1, -0.4, -12.5; median absolute about 5%) I set abs_move at 9, because a third guide raise is the likely swing line. p_up is 54, a slight lean from one sector proxy: prediction-market volume rose about 70% QoQ in Q3 and set an October record, which feeds the Digital Finance line that drove Q2. Three things hold p_up near 50: the H2 take-rate and gross-margin warning, a 58% run since the last print, and the stock trading above the average price target. The findings sum (+0.3) and the scaled number (+0.72) agree in sign and are both small.

findings.finding: Prediction-market volume, the driver of Riskified's Digital Finance category, accelerated through Q3 and into Q4. Industry volume was about $188B in Q3 2026, about +70% QoQ and about 21x YoY (CryptoRank via Phemex, 2026-10-06). Polymarket US weekly trade volume rose 190% between the weeks ending Sep 6 and Oct 11, and Kalshi set a record $19.03B week on Oct 5-11. Polymarket was reported (WSJ via crypto.news, 2026-09-20) to have brought in Riskified as its outside anti-fraud provider by May. Digital Finance (event contracts and gaming) grew about 180% YoY in Q2 and led the quarter's 22% growth. The Q3 framing of about 27% growth was given on 2026-08-12, before most of the NFL-season ramp, and the Q4 guide implies only +10% to +20%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue acceleration plus a raised FY guide bought +22.4% on 2026-08-12 (close $5.27 to $6.45, wallstsmart). The 2026-05-13 beat with a raise bought +1.3%. A beat on 2026-03-04 sold -5.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Riskified does not disclose Digital Finance revenue or customer names. The Polymarket link is single-source press, not a company statement. Sell-side still sits at a 'Reduce' consensus with a $7.17 average target, below spot. Earnings Whispers calls FY consensus of about $380m stale against a $400m+ guide. If the market had mapped the Q3-Q4 prediction-market surge onto RSKD, the FY guide-raise expectation would be visible in estimates and targets, and they still sit below the guide.
findings.independence: Polymarket US and Kalshi weekly volumes: https://defirate.com/news/kalshi-hits-record-19-billion-week-as-polymarket-us-triples-fall-trade-volume/ (2026-10-12). Polymarket-Riskified link: https://crypto.news/polymarket-hit-by-alleged-10m-stolen-card-fraud/ (2026-09-20). Digital Finance +180% in Q2: https://finviz.com/news/414749/riskified-must-prove-its-growth-surge-can-survive-thinner-margins-and-easing-take-rates. This is a proxy: the company has not confirmed Q3 Digital Finance volumes. Net of the rest of the company: EMEA grew only about 3% and fashion and luxury about 4% in Q2, and the World Cup and NBA Finals boost to Tickets in Q2 does not repeat, so the core book has to hold roughly flat for this to show.

findings.finding: Guide arithmetic. FY2026 revenue guide is $400-410m, H1 revenue was $187.0m (6-K), and Q3 is framed at about $104m (about +27%). That leaves Q4 at $109-119m, +10% to +20% YoY on $99.3m, a sharp slowdown from Q3. A hold of the FY range at the Q3 print would therefore read as Q4 deceleration. A raise only needs Q4 growth near Q3's pace.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The second FY raise on 2026-08-12 (midpoint +$25m) went with +22.4%. The first raise on 2026-05-13 went with +1.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The arithmetic is public and the stock is up 58% since the print, which is what a market expecting another raise looks like. What is not priced is the reported FY consensus, about $380m per Earnings Whispers, below even the low end of the guide. If estimates had caught up, consensus would sit at $405m or above.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 revenue of $99.3m: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260304262574/en/Riskified-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results (2026-03-04). Shares the Q3 bar with finding 1. This finding is the guide-shape mechanism and finding 1 is the demand evidence, so they are distinct facts.

findings.finding: Quality-of-beat risk. Q2 non-GAAP gross margin fell to 46% from 50%, and GAAP gross profit grew only 13% against 22% revenue growth. Management blamed lower-margin ticketing and newer, higher-risk merchants, and warned that take rates should compress in H2. The higher-risk merchant set includes prediction-market deposits: Polymarket US saw a February 2026 card-fraud wave in which more than 80% of deposits were rejected at the peak. So the same volume driver that lifts revenue can push gross margin below 46%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2025 print (Aug 2025) fell about 12.5% on 'profitability concerns despite meeting estimates' (itiger Stock Track). In Q2 2026 a 400bp gross-margin drop was overridden by revenue growth and the raise (+22%).
findings.why_not_priced: The warning is public, but consensus revenue of +27% sits above Q2's 22% while GMV grew only 13% in Q2. A compressing take rate would therefore have to be offset by faster GMV. If that were priced, Q3 revenue estimates would sit nearer GMV growth plus a smaller take-rate uplift.
findings.independence: Q2 6-K gross margin of 46% against 49-50%: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001851112/000162828026055937/exhibit991-q22026.htm. Polymarket fraud history: https://crypto.news/polymarket-hit-by-alleged-10m-stolen-card-fraud/. This shares the prediction-market driver with finding 1 but lands on a different line (margin, not revenue), so both can be true at once.

findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. It is filed because the upside skew says the option market leans the other way. The case against the skew is that low short interest (about 1.2%, DTC about 1.2) means no squeeze fuel, and the call-heavy book can unwind on an in-line print.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers: up nearly 40% since the last report at $8.48, sentiment moved to mildly bullish (https://finviz.com/news/414749/riskified-must-prove-its-growth-surge-can-survive-thinner-margins-and-easing-take-rates). Baseline: skew -17.22, P/C OI 0.17.

findings.finding: Buyback capacity and the likelihood of a new authorization. Riskified bought 13.7M shares for $63.9M in Q2, and shares outstanding are down 26% since the program began. About $105.6m of authority stood after the June 4 $75m add-on, less buying through late June. Cash and investments were $223.6m with no debt, and FY FCF is targeted above $40m. The company has repeatedly paired new authorizations with prints, and remaining authority after Q3 buying is likely thin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean isolation. Past authorizations came with the release or a few weeks after, so their effect is mixed into the print reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Whether a new authorization comes at the print is unknown. A finsee.ai review calls the cash decline from about $300m to $223.6m a 'rapid liquidity drain', so the market may instead expect the buyback pace to slow, and a new authorization would cut against that.

findings.finding: Insider activity into the print is routine. Ravi Kumaraswami (President, Worldwide Field Ops) sold 65,000 shares at a $8.36 weighted average on 2026-10-15 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-03-16, keeping 1.42M. CEO Eido Gal's 2026-10-05 Form 4 is tax withholding only (34,391 shares at $7.93, code F).
findings.why_not_priced: It is public on EDGAR. The sale is pre-planned and small, so it carries little information, which is why it is sized near zero.

findings.finding: Founder 13G/A filings as of 2026-09-30 use 112,550,023 Class A shares outstanding, against 91.8M Class A (132.0M total with Class B) at 2026-06-30. That implies about 20.7M of Class B converted to Class A in Q3. Founders still hold Class B convertible within 60 days: Eido Gal 9.11M of his 13.71M beneficial (11.3%), Assaf Feldman 11.39M (9.4%). The Class B count at Sep 30 is not disclosed, so the Q3 buyback pace cannot be read from this.
findings.why_not_priced: It is not in the wire copy. Conversion of Class B (likely by non-founder holders) can precede selling, but nothing shows sales. The total share count, and so the Q3 buyback, will only be visible in the release.

baseline_tension: Finding 1 agrees with the upside skew and the run-up, so part of it is likely priced. The positioning and margin findings cut against them, which is why p_up sits at 54 and not 58.
lessons_applied: Lessons 5 and 9: cut the prediction-market finding from +2.0 to +1.5. It is a sector proxy with no company confirmation, and Digital Finance is one category, so it is sized net of the slow EMEA and fashion book and the World Cup/NBA tickets boost that does not repeat.
Lesson 6: cut the guide-arithmetic finding from +1.0 to +0.6. It rests on the company's own published guide, which the market can compute.
Lesson 7: cut the negative positioning finding from -1.0 to -0.7. Its sign is against an upside skew (-17), and the only case against the skew is low short interest plus a call-heavy book.
